summary: Sandbox personal data must stay in a separated, isolated and protected environment with authorised access only, sharing limits, no measures or decisions affecting data subjects, and no impairment of data-protection rights.

summary: Providers or prospective providers may conduct real-world testing of Annex III high-risk AI systems outside sandboxes only under Article 60 and a real-world testing plan before market placement or putting into service, without affecting prohibitions or required ethical review.
quote: "Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes may be conducted by providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, in accordance with this Article and the real-world testing plan referred to in this Article, without prejudice to the prohibitions under Article 5."
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI vendors testing Annex III high-risk systems, including justice-related systems.

summary: Real-world testing may occur only if Article 60(4) conditions are met, including plan approval, registration, Union establishment or representation, transfer safeguards, time limits, vulnerable-person protection, deployer role agreements, consent or law-enforcement safeguards, oversight and reversibility.
quote: "Providers or prospective providers may conduct the testing in real world conditions only where all of the following conditions are met:"
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI providers and deployers participating in real-world tests.

summary: Testing subjects or their representatives may withdraw without detriment and request deletion of personal data, and Member States must give market surveillance authorities powers to obtain information, inspect and check testing.
quote: "Any subjects of the testing in real world conditions, or their legally designated representative, as appropriate, may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time by revoking their informed consent and may request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data."
legal_practice_note: Medium where legal-AI real-world testing includes individuals as test subjects.

summary: Serious incidents during real-world testing must be reported to the market surveillance authority, immediate mitigation or suspension/termination and recall procedures must follow, suspension or termination and final outcomes must be notified, and providers remain liable for damage.
quote: "Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73. legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI providers conducting high-risk real-world tests.

summary: For Article 60 real-world testing, freely given informed consent must be obtained before participation after concise, clear, relevant and understandable information on nature, conditions, rights, reversal arrangements and identification/contact details.
quote: "For the purpose of testing in real world conditions under Article 60, freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing and after their having been duly informed with concise, clear, relevant, and understandable information regarding:"

summary: Informed consent for Article 60 real-world testing must be dated and documented, and a copy must be given to the test subject or legal representative.
quote: "The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative."
legal_practice_note: Medium for legal-AI real-world testing documentation.

summary: Member States must support SMEs, start-ups, deployers and relevant public authorities through priority sandbox access, tailored awareness and training, advice channels, participation in standardisation, and proportionate conformity-assessment fees.

legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: The European Artificial Intelligence Board is established with one Member State representative, EDPS observer participation, AI Office attendance without voting, and possible invitations to relevant authorities, bodies or experts.

legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: Board representatives must adopt rules of procedure, the Board must establish standing sub-groups and operate objectively and impartially, and the AI Office must provide the secretariat, convene meetings and prepare agendas.
quote: "The designated representatives of the Member States shall adopt the Board’s rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority. quote: "The advisory forum shall draw up its rules of procedure. It shall elect two co-chairs from among its members, in accordance with criteria set out in paragraph 2. The term of office of the co-chairs shall be two years, renewable once."
legal_practice_note: Institutional governance mechanics; indirect relevance to legal practices through oversight and guidance.

summary: The Commission must establish a scientific panel by implementing act, selecting experts with AI expertise, independence from providers, and ability to act diligently, accurately and objectively.
